root_cause.contract: AI content guard returns approve, flag, or block; flag means ambiguous or review-required content.
root_cause.provider_behavior: ContentModerationProviderImpl returns flag when the AI moderation service is unavailable.
root_cause.defect: Five Monolith consumers rejected only block, allowing flag results to continue into persistence/publication. FE social composers also warned on flag and continued, while cook-post and recipe guard callers did not require explicit approval.
root_cause.failure_before_fix: PostServiceTest.createPersonalPostRejectsFlaggedContentBeforeSaving failed because the flagged create completed without throwing.

change.decision: Monolith post, comment, reply, chat, and story-reply paths plus FE post, comment, reply, quick-post, cook-post, and recipe-publish paths now require action=approve; failures, null results, flag, block, and unknown actions stop before persistence/publication.
change.provider_log: The AI-unavailable log now says content is rejected, not held in a review queue that does not exist.
change.review_queue: Not implemented; flagged content is rejected with the existing moderation error.

frontend_regressions.lint: passed with no ESLint warnings or errors
frontend_regressions.production_build: passed with temporary Google Font fixtures after Next's Google Font parser failed on the external response
frontend_regressions.flagged_message: Updated post, comment, reply, and quick-post messages to state flagged content was not published.

browser_context.result: Headed installed Chrome passed 2/2 across desktop and iPhone-sized Chromium; it verifies block/flag/unexpected action refusal, the flagged rejection message, and approved post/session-link/XP request construction.
browser_context.limitation: Playwright intercepts all /api/v1/** calls with test fixtures; it is not a live FE-to-Monolith transaction.

limitations: Maven tests use mocks and do not verify production provider availability or deployment configuration.
Flagged content is rejected, not queued for moderator review.
Kafka event delivery and persisted social-feed visibility were not exercised in a deployed system.
